chunks: 4829 - Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abān and others, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There was a man in the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله named Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, and he had a wife named Khawlah bint al-Mundhir. One day he said to her, “You are to me like the back of my mother.” Then he regretted it immediately and said to her, “O woman, I think that you have become unlawful for me.” So she came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said, “O Messenger of Allah, my husband said to me, ‘You are to me like the back of my mother,’ and this statement in former times used to make a woman unlawful to her husband.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to her, “O woman, I think that you have indeed become unlawful for him.” Then the woman raised her hand to the sky and said, “I complain to You of separation from my husband.” Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: “O Muḥammad:”

“Allah has indeed heard the speech of the woman who disputes with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears the dialogue between you both. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. Those among you who pronounce ẓihār against their wives—they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. Indeed they surely utter an objectionable word and a falsehood, and indeed Allah is surely Pardoning, Forgiving.”
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the expiation regarding that, and said:

“And those who pronounce ẓihār against their wives, then go back on what they said, then the freeing of a slave before the two touch one another—that is what you are admonished by, and Allah is All-Aware of what you do. Then whoever does not find, then fasting for two consecutive months before the two touch one another; then whoever is unable, then feeding sixty poor persons.”

key_terms.إِطْعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا: feeding sixty poor persons as the third form of expiation
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةَ: the expiation required for this unlawful utterance
key_terms.تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ: freeing a slave as the first form of expiation
key_terms.تُجَادِلُكَ: she argues or pleads with you regarding her case
key_terms.صِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: fasting two consecutive months as the second form of expiation
key_terms.كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي: like the back of my mother, the formula of ẓihār
key_terms.يُظَاهِرُونَ: they pronounce ẓihār, declaring their wives unlawful by likening them to their mothers

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and expiation for ẓihār in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the occasion of revelation concerning ẓihār, when a husband likened his wife to his mother, and Allah rejected this pre-Islamic formula as false speech. The passage also establishes the kaffarah for ẓihār: freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty needy persons.
